definitions.explanation: describes the manner of crying with loud sobs or wails

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧おいおい⟦{泣|な}いた→泣く：00655_naku⟧。
⟦{悲|かな}しくて→悲しい：00783_kanashii⟧おいおい⟦{泣|な}いて→泣く：00655_naku⟧しまった。
examples.english: I was so sad that I burst into tears.

examples.japanese: ⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧おいおい⟦{泣|な}いている→泣く：00655_naku⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧がいた。
examples.english: There was someone bawling while watching the movie.

notes:
USAGE:
An adverb for the sound and manner of loud, uncontrolled crying, used with ⟦{泣|な}く→泣く：00655_naku⟧: おいおい⟦{泣|な}く→泣く：00655_naku⟧, おいおい⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{泣|な}く→泣く：00655_naku⟧ (to bawl).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦しくしく→しくしく：05373_shikushiku⟧ - sobbing quietly
- ⟦わんわん→わんわん：05428_wanwan⟧ - crying loudly (like a child)
- ⟦めそめそ→めそめそ：05772_mesomeso⟧ - whimpering, sniffling

WATCH OUT:
The interjection おいおい ("hey, hey!", "come on!", as in おいおい、⟦{冗談|じょうだん}→冗談：03347_joudan⟧だろ) and the adverb ⟦{追々|おいおい}→追々：31199_oioi⟧ (gradually, in due course) are different words.
